rules.Pitch_Types.description: True surface with predictable bounce; best for batting.
Fresh grass, lateral movement and strong new-ball assistance.
Hard early surface that becomes slower and increasingly supports spin.
Loose surface with sharp turn, variable bounce and difficult stroke play.
Firm surface with steep carry; rewards fast bowling but allows shots once set.
Low-paced surface where timing is difficult and cutters/spin are effective.

rules.Stadium_Conditions.notes: Spin-friendly venue baseline; pitch choice still controls the prepared surface.
Large-ground simulation baseline with balanced outfield.
Quick outfield with a stronger evening-dew chance.
Fast outfield, smaller boundaries and strong evening dew.
Balanced venue with relatively low dew.
High-scoring baseline with fast outfield and altitude assistance.

rules.Weather_Conditions.description: Dry and stable conditions with balanced assistance.
Cloud cover helps swing and seam bowling.
Moist air adds movement and increases evening dew.
Heat reduces movement, helps spin and drains stamina.
Wind creates variable movement and slightly restricts boundaries.
Damp conditions strongly help pace movement and slow the outfield.

rules.Consistency_Profiles.description: Performs close to rating most often; minor weaknesses still matter.
Reliable player with occasional poor matches.
Frequent swings between good and poor performances.
Highly unpredictable with a wide performance range.

rules.Batting_Approaches.description: Protects the wicket, allows rotation and sharply reduces boundary attempts.
Prioritises singles and doubles with slightly reduced wicket risk.
Strongly increases boundary attempts while accepting higher dismissal risk.

rules.Bowling_Approaches.description: Attacks for wickets but concedes more boundaries when execution fails.
Prioritises dots and boundary prevention over wicket-taking.
Uses the bowler's normal attributes without tactical modifiers.
Uses pace and bounce; dangerous when inaccurate or predictable.
Strong death option; missed yorkers become high-risk full tosses.
Separate pace variation; effective when disguised and accurately controlled.
Uses changes in flight, pace and turn rather than a pace slower ball.

rules.Ball_Outcome_Rules.description: Higher boundary opportunity while fielding restrictions apply.
More strike rotation with controlled boundary frequency.
Higher boundary and wicket rates under aggressive play.

rules.Fielding_Presets.description: Two catchers with two legal boundary fielders.
Protects common gaps while keeping two fielders outside.
Leg-side boundary trap for short-ball plans.
Five boundary riders protect missed death deliveries.
Cuts singles and protects major spin-hitting zones.
Legal balanced field usable throughout the innings.
Maximum legal boundary protection outside the powerplay.

rules.Dismissal_Rules.description: Movement increases LBW and caught-behind chances.
Medium pace produces more outfield catches.
Off-spin adds LBW and stumping chances.
Leg-spin has the highest base stumping chance.
Left-arm spin balances LBW, catches and stumpings.
Short-ball plans create catches behind and in the deep.
Accurate yorkers mainly produce bowled and LBW dismissals.
Flight and turn increase catches and stumpings.

rules.Delivery_Rules.description: Attacking lengths around the stumps with controlled wicket-seeking risk.
Targets safe lines and hard-to-hit lengths.
Neutral distribution based mainly on bowler attributes.
Body-line short-ball plan with execution risk.
Targets yorkers; misses become full or hittable deliveries.
Disguised pace-off delivery with varied sensible lengths.
Changes flight, pace and turn while maintaining a controlled length.

rules.Shot_Rules.description: Safe defensive response that strongly lowers dismissal risk.
Leaves deliveries outside the scoring area.
Ground or aerial drive through cover and straight regions.
Efficient leg-side rotation and boundary option.
Uses bowler pace to target areas behind the wicket.
Creates room to hit over the off side.
Back-foot scoring shot for controlled rotation.
Failure outcome produced by poor execution, pressure or movement.
